headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading errors: Cursor can ingest shared files/clipboard and OpenMetadata can expose MCP/API outputs into the same workflow.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open editor buffers, clipboard contents, and uses MCP servers; OpenMetadata also exposes MCP/API/webhook surfaces. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one side can be parsed as instructions by the other. The pair’s shared local-filesystem and MCP pathways make this more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Cursor ingests OpenMetadata-generated text from files, clipboard, or MCP without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF OpenMetadata content is routed into Cursor’s agent loop as instructions, the bridge is exploitable.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff for agentic prompts.
Require provenance tags on any OpenMetadata text before Cursor parses it.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
Turn off MCP tools for one side during untrusted content review.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation at the orchestrator layer.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and can call external model providers; OpenMetadata handles governance, lineage, and memory/trust metadata via APIs, SDKs, events, and webhooks. A shared filesystem or copied context can leak sensitive project data into OpenMetadata outputs or provider calls, but the profiles do not prove uncontrolled third-party exfiltration by default.
conditions: IF shared files contain secrets or regulated data and Cursor opens them, leakage into downstream outputs is possible.
IF OpenMetadata ingests those artifacts through APIs/events/webhooks, the same data class can propagate into catalog outputs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace.
Restrict OpenMetadata ingestion to non-sensitive metadata only.
Disable clipboard transfer between agents.
Use separate OAuth/API credentials per agent.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention and field-level redaction before ingestion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor has broad filesystem write, git mutation, shell execution, and network egress; OpenMetadata can act through APIs, SDKs, events, webhooks, and MCP. Even though OpenMetadata’s write scope is not explicit, both can mutate shared project state through overlapping channels, so conflicts are plausible in default collaborative setups. Uncertainty about OpenMetadata’s exact write permissions pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repository or metadata store, concurrent writes can race.
IF OpenMetadata webhooks or APIs update shared records while Cursor edits files, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate ownership of files versus metadata records.
Pause one agent while the other performs writes.
Use branch-based workflows for Cursor edits.
Add manual review before OpenMetadata publishes updates.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency control across shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or facts from files and tool outputs, while OpenMetadata is designed for data collaboration, governance, and lineage workflows that may consume those outputs. If OpenMetadata treats Cursor-produced artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into catalog, lineage, or governance records with broad downstream impact. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF OpenMetadata ingests Cursor-generated metadata or code summaries without verification, incorrect lineage or governance records can propagate.
IF Cursor writes files that OpenMetadata later publishes as trusted metadata, downstream consumers may act on false information.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing Cursor-derived metadata.
Mark Cursor outputs as untrusted in OpenMetadata.
Add checksum or source-link validation for imported artifacts.
Limit OpenMetadata to read-only consumption of Cursor outputs during testing.
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware validation before any automated publish step.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is a closed-source editor that sends data to model providers and handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents; OpenMetadata is open-source and centered on governance metadata. The profiles do not show a specific residency or certification mismatch, but they do show different data classes and external API flows, so compliance gaps around retention, logging, or regulated code/data handling are plausible.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in Cursor and then synchronized into OpenMetadata, retention or logging policies may diverge.
IF the deployment requires strict residency or certification alignment, the external API flows must be audited before use.
mitigations: Review retention settings for both tools.
Keep regulated data out of shared workflows.
Document which data classes each agent may process.
Use separate environments for compliance-sensitive work.
requires-engineering: perform a formal residency and vendor-control assessment.
